concept.title: Topics, maps and bookmaps
concept.shortdesc: Each page is a topic in its own file. A map arranges topics into the site navigation and defines keys; a bookmap arranges them into a PDF publication.

section.title: Topics
section.p: A topic file holds one topic: topic, concept, task, reference, glossentry or troubleshooting. Its root element needs an id, and every id inside one topic must be unique.
section.codeblock: <task id="install-cli"> <title>Install the CLI from a checkout</title> <shortdesc>Build the opend command and check that it runs.</shortdesc> <taskbody> <steps> <step><cmd>Clone the repository.</cmd></step> </steps> </taskbody> </task>
section.p: The page URL is the file's path without its extension, so topics/start/install-cli.dita is served at /topics/start/install-cli.html. Keep file names stable: links from outside the site depend on them.
A topic may contain nested topics, which render as sections of the same page and can be linked with file.dita#nested-id. A <dita> wrapper may hold several topics; the first is the page.

section.title: Maps
section.p: The root map named by map in opend.config.yaml defines the navigation, in document order:
section.codeblock: <map> <title>OpenD Documentation</title> <mapref href="keys.ditamap"/> <topicref href="../topics/overview.dita"/> <topichead navtitle="Get started"> <topicref href="../topics/start/install-cli.dita"/> </topichead> <topichead navtitle="Embedded help" product="embed"> <topicref href="../topics/help/help-overview.dita"/> </topichead> </map>

ul.li: topicref adds a topic. Without a navtitle, the navigation shows the topic's title as the reader sees it, so a conditional phrase in a title stays filtered.
topichead adds a heading with a navtitle and no page. A heading with nothing visible under it is left out of that reader's navigation.
topicgroup, frontmatter and backmatter group entries without adding a level.
mapref (or a topicref to a .ditamap) includes a submap at that point. Its entries and keys are merged in; reference cycles are errors.
toc="no" publishes a topic without listing it in the navigation.
keydef and processing-role="resource-only" define keys without adding navigation. See .

section.p: A topic is published to a reader only when a navigation entry they can see points at it and the topic's own root passes their filter. Filtering attributes on a map entry apply to everything under it.

section.title: Bookmaps
section.p: A bookmap listed under publications becomes a PDF. Its booktitle/mainbooktitle is the publication title, and chapter, part and appendix entries work like topicref. A bookmap resolves keys in its own keyspace, so pull shared keys in with a mapref. See .
